locator.section: web/www/missa/Latin/Ordo/Prayers.txt [Per eumdem], section line 107; full conclusion and R. Amen. at lines 108–109

entries.claim: The literal $Per eumdem directive in Nat2-0.txt resolves to this full conclusion and Amen response. The equal-text Per eundem alias at lines 111–113 is not the invoked section.

locator.section: web/www/missa/Latin/Tempora/Nat2-0.txt [Secreta], section line 59; body line 60 and $Per eumdem reference line 61

entries.claim: The pinned Latin Mass file supplies the Secret body and its literal $Per eumdem reference. The conclusion is separately resolved from the declared Prayers.txt dependency; this file alone is not a continuous full-text witness.

locator.section: Sanctissimi Nominis Iesu, Secreta; body and abbreviated Per eundem Dominum cue

entries.claim: The approved Benziger printing gives the 37-word Secret body followed by the abbreviated Per eundem Dominum cue. It does not print the complete expanded conclusion on this page.

locator.section: Postcommunio continuing Monday after the first Sunday of the Passion, above the Tuesday heading; Dominum nostrum through Deus.

entries.claim: This separate Postcommunion prints the accented middle conclusion, including no comma after Christum and the colon and uppercase Qui after tuum, ending with Deus. The composite uses Dominum nostrum through Deus.; this page supplies neither eundem nor the final duration or Amen.

locator.section: Top conclusion and response before the Nativity preface dialogue; Per omnia saecula saeculorum. R. Amen.

entries.claim: The top chant line prints Per omnia saecula saeculorum and the response Amen. The composite joins musical syllable divisions and omits the response marker. Only these five words are used; the Nativity preface dialogue and body are excluded.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 115 a; Father-addressed oration conclusion

entries.claim: RG 115 a supplies the full Father-addressed conclusion, ending with Amen. It controls the expansion rule, not the selected composite transcript's accents or its accidental seams.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 115 b; mention of the Son in an oration addressed to the Father

entries.claim: RG 115 b prescribes Per eundem Dominum nostrum, etc., ut supra when an oration addressed to the Father mentions the Son at its beginning. The Secret names the Son within its body, and the printed cue Per eúndem Dóminum on p. 35 shows this form; the end-mention rule of 115 c is not used here.

locator.section: RG 480–481, 511 d/i, 513–514; Ordo Missae rubric and chant formula after the secrets

entries.claim: The final secret has an audible Per omnia saecula saeculorum followed by the response Amen. Collects and postcommunions are priestly orations with a separate response. These rules determine the modeled boundaries, not the completeness of a date-specific commemoration inventory.
